text:
ana: Pushed a docs PR that consolidates dedicated provisioning migration notes + adds a small Go SDK snippet for tenant labels. Can someone skim for API accuracy and wording? PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/512
omar: On it. Which APIs did you call in the Go snippet?
ana: (typo) ana: It's using client.ReserveCapacity(...) but I also included the older allocateTenant example as a note for historical context. I'm happy to remove the old one if it's confusing.
rachel: Please remove deprecated example — it'll confuse readers. Also, add a one-line 'what happens on overcommit' explanation under autoscale.
ana: Removed deprecated call. New Go snippet: ```go
package main

import (
  "os"
  "github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/redwood"
)

func main() {
  client := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
  _, err := client.ReserveCapacity("tenant-42", redwood.ReservationOptions{
    GPUs: 4,
    Labels: map[string]string{"team": "recs", "env": "staging"},
  })
  if err != nil {
    panic(err)
  }
}
```
omar: Snippet looks correct but rename ReserveCapacity -> ReserveCapacitySync in docs if the client method is blocking in our SDK v0.9.2. Check compatibility note.
docs-bot: md-lint: line 220: long line >120 chars in migration.md (suggested wrap).
infra-bot: link-check: handbook/provisioning.md#isolation-example -> 404. Suggest handbook/provisioning.md#tenant-isolation instead.
rachel: For the autoscale section add two tiny examples: 1) cooldown_seconds: 45 for bursty inference, 2) cooldown_seconds: 300 for steady traffic. Also clarify preemption vs eviction: "preemption: provider-initiated reclaim (may cause SLA adjustments); eviction: node-level reclaim due to infra maintenance or tenant misbehavior. Example: Preemption -> spot GPU loss; Eviction -> node drained for kernel patch." Keep wording non-legal.
ana: Added both cooldown examples and the preemption/eviction paragraph. Wrote a small SLA note: "Adjusted SLA = Base SLA - RegionPreemptionAllowance (see table below)." Left a TODO to populate the table per-region.
omar: Product asks to document fallback policy key used by Dedicated: fallback_policy: compatible_fallback with example config. Add a note about canary: canary uses 'rollout_fraction' in provisioning metadata.
rachel: One last ask: include an isolation decorator YAML snippet showing tenant_isolation: strict and example of label enforcement. 
ana: Added YAML samples: ```yaml
provisioning:
  mode: dedicated
  fallback_policy: compatible_fallback
  autoscale:
    policy: target_utilization
    cooldown_seconds: 45
  rollout:
    canary:
      enabled: true
      rollout_fraction: 0.05
tenant_isolation: strict # strict: per-tenant node isolation, best-effort enforcement
```
docs-bot: spellcheck: 'rollout_fraction' OK, 'tenant_isolation' OK.
infra-bot: CI note: example config references 'strict' but back-end supports 'hard' or 'soft' historically. Please reconcile with infra.
omar: Prefer 'hard'/'soft' in docs to match infra API. 
rachel: I'll update the wording to say "hard/soft" and include the mapping note. Also left a PR comment asking to add the region table placeholder.
ana: Great. I pushed updates and replied to the infra comment clarifying the mapping. Final diff: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/512/files. If CI/link-check pass I'll merge after a final doc-approvers tick. /cc @omar @rachel
